## TL;DR
Close-outs now validate up to `maxParallelValidations` queued jobs at once (default 2, range 1–8). Publishing to `main` stays strictly serial in queue order, and a job whose base moved is re-validated before it can publish. This final pass was hand-fixed by the driver: main was merged in (conflicts with #1276 resolved in `integration-orchestrator.ts`, `server.ts` and `integration-pipeline-ui.ts`, keeping both sides) and the last review findings were fixed: only the parked wait is excluded from the timeout budget, a parked publisher is no longer labelled stalled, a crashing run backs off and is eventually failed instead of retrying forever, and crashes are no longer swallowed.

## Work and rationale
- Scheduling is a pure function, `selectCloseOutStarts` in `integration-job.ts`, so the server pump and tests share one definition. A job in `publishing` starts only when it holds the publish turn, so only the queue head can merge; a job that finishes validating early parks with its candidate intact. Per-run state lives on a fresh `CloseOutOrchestrator` per task.
- `server.ts`: `CloseOutScheduler` pumps on enqueue and after each run. The orchestrator factory now also carries #1276's step/host-change callback (`() => emitIntegration()`). `runCloseOut` now rethrows a crash after its normal bookkeeping instead of swallowing it, and a new `failCrashedCloseOut` fails a job whose run keeps crashing so it leaves the queue.
- `close-out-scheduler.ts`: a run that throws backs off (5s, 10s) and is retried a bounded number of times (`MAX_RUN_CRASHES` = 3), then `onGiveUp` fails the job; a given-up job is never restarted while it still sits in the queue, so a failed hand-off cannot become a crash loop. A clean run clears the count.
- `integration-orchestrator.ts`: when a parked publisher gets its turn, the budget anchor moves forward only by the time spent parked (`shiftBudgetAnchorPastWait`), so time already spent validating still counts and a job cannot exceed the configured ceiling by parking. This relies on `readJob` now returning `budgetMonotonicStartNs` (from #1276).
- `integration-pipeline-ui.ts`: a publisher parked for its turn reads "validated · waiting for its publish turn" and is never labelled stalled, in the card, drawer and bar copy. Merged cleanly with #1276's attempt/host/retry-reason label helpers.
- Config key `maxParallelValidations` is wired through defaults, loadConfig, the Settings schema, supported keys and `user-docs/configuration.md`; `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` describes the scheduler, the publish turn and the stale-base rule.
- Tests: scheduler crash backoff, give-up and recovery; the budget shift helper (excludes only the wait, never past now, null cases); parked copy not stalled; existing parallel, parked-publisher, cancel and timeout suites still pass.

## Latest round (driver hand-fix)
- Every write to main outside a publish is now taken under the publish locks (`withMainCheckout`): the gate-duration bookkeeping commit and the failure repair (review-lock restore plus board status).
- The parked wait is measured on the monotonic clock: the job records `parkedAtNs` when it enters `publishing` and clears it once used, so a restart cannot shift the budget twice.
- A job that keeps crashing is failed through the orchestrator's normal failure path (`failCrashed`: candidate teardown, review-lock restore, board status). If that hand-off fails the scheduler does not abandon the job: it backs off and hands off again on the next crash.
- Parallel jobs in the status snapshot now carry attempt, step, host, retry reason and their own stall flag; a parked publisher is never flagged stale in the snapshot or in `GET /integration-job` (`isParkedPublisher`).

## Approaches tried
Kept the existing fail-closed stale-base guard rather than a cheaper re-merge, which could not be proven safe without running the gate. For crashes, fail the job after bounded backoff rather than retrying forever, and keep the given-up state sticky so a failed fail-hand-off cannot loop.

## Challenges and blockers
Earlier rounds failed handoff on timing-sensitive remote tests under load and on an unrelated config-test failure; those pass locally through the repo's test wrapper. The branch also conflicted with #1276 because both rewrote the close-out progress and orchestrator code. No end-to-end test runs a real crashing orchestrator; the scheduler and helpers are unit-tested and the server wiring is covered by typecheck and the existing parallel and cancel suites.

## Key learnings
A scheduler that restarts a failing job immediately needs three things: backoff, a bound, and a way to take the job out of the queue, or one bad job blocks everything behind it. A budget that resets on resume is not a budget; exclude only the wait.
